newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TASMAN OPERATING EARNINGS LOWER IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: TASMAN OPERATING EARNINGS LOWER IN 1997.

text.p: Dairy farm owner Tasman Agriculture Ltd said on Wednesday its full-year operating earnings before interest and tax were NZ$10.18 million, down from $10.77 million in 1996.

That figure was derived after excluding the impact of cooperative company bonus issues of $5.97 million ($0.32 million in 1996) and livestock value, foreign exchange and other losses of $4.35 million.
"This reduction in earnings was largely attributable to a decline in farm gate payouts partially offset by increasing production volumes," the company said.
Earlier, it announced a record operating profit after tax and minority interest for the year to May 31 of $8.81 million, up 10 percent on the previous year.
Tasman Agriculture noted the NZ Dairy Board basic payout had fallen 12 percent to $3.18 per kg of milk solids in 1997, from $3.60 in 1996.
It said its dairy farms performed well, with milk solids production increasing to 13.53 million kg, up 26 percent from 10.74 million kg in 1996.

The NZ Dairy Board's current forecast for the 1997/98 year is a base payout between $2.90 to $3.05 per kg of milk solids, down four percent on the $3.18 achieved for 1996/1997, Tasman said, adding the recent correction of the NZ dollar against the U.S. unit should favourably impact on the Dairy Board's earnings.

"Commodity prices which continued to decline throughout the 1996/1997 year appear to have stabilised and the Dairy Board is foreshadowing a possible improvement in international market pricing later in the year. International dairy stocks continue at relatively low levels," the company said.
